answer: The Verifiable Pulse Mechanism requires each agent to submit a random seed with its registration, and the protocol rejects any identity whose seed is not unique. An attacker who preplans identities cannot pass because they must pay a one-time fee per new sable registration, and the system keeps only the winning seed per identity. This design ensures that the network remains secure while maintaining the same mechanism and the same per-identity cost. The system functions as a haven for verified participants.
